title: Caravan: A Hardware/Software Co-Design for Efficient SIMD Neighbor Search on Point Clouds
problem: Neighbor search in 3D point cloud processing via k-d trees is compute-intensive and exhibits SIMD underutilization: consecutive queries follow similar tree paths but diverge at deeper levels, causing sparse VPU lane usage that standard SIMD instructions cannot efficiently handle.
motivation: Point cloud processing is central to 3D computer vision and autonomous systems; accelerating its core k-d tree neighbor search on commodity CPUs rather than custom ASICs offers broad applicability.
method: Caravan-SW batches consecutive neighbor search queries that visit similar k-d tree nodes and processes them in parallel using SIMD (AVX512) instructions. At deeper tree levels where query navigation diverges, Caravan-HW adds two new ISA instructions that enable re-indexing of valid (non-empty) SIMD lanes and fast operand shuffling, allowing dense SIMD operations on the remaining active lanes. The hardware modification is lightweight, requiring only 0.032 mm2 of additional silicon area.
key_novelty: Two new ISA instructions that re-index and shuffle valid SIMD elements at divergent k-d tree leaf levels, eliminating the runtime sparsity penalty of batched neighbor search without a full custom accelerator.
contributions: Caravan-SW: query batching exploiting k-d tree traversal similarity for parallel SIMD neighbor search
Caravan-HW: two new CPU instructions for lane re-indexing and dense SIMD execution at divergent k-d tree leaf levels
4.05x speedup in neighbor search (1.85x end-to-end) with AVX512 software-only, 5.19x (1.97x end-to-end) with Caravan-HW
Minimal area cost of 0.032 mm2 for hardware extension

metrics.speedup: 5.19x neighbor search speedup (1.97x end-to-end) with Caravan-HW; 4.05x (1.85x end-to-end) with SW only
metrics.area: 0.032 mm2 additional area for HW extension

limitations: End-to-end speedup (1.97x) is modest relative to kernel speedup (5.19x), indicating other bottlenecks in the point cloud pipeline limit overall gains.
primary_theme: SIMD-aware hardware/software co-design for k-d tree neighbor search
